computer-assisted psychotherapies can be as effective and acceptable as standard psychotherapies in the treatment of depression, and that the effects are maintained for at least six months.

the TLP program, which is based on cognitive-behavior therapy, is as effective as CBT, as measured by the Beck Depression Inventory and Beck Anxiety Inventory, and is equally well liked by participants, as measured by a satisfaction survey.

computer-assisted psychotherapies (CAPs) are as effective as face-to-face psychotherapies in the treatment of anxiety and depression, but they are more cost-effective and can reach a wider range of people, particularly those who are geographically isolated, have a busy life, are socially isolated, and/or have difficulty in attending face-to-face therapy.

the development and testing of computer-assisted therapy programs for anxiety and depression in a clinical setting, with a focus on the individualization and tailoring of treatment to the needs and goals of each patient.
developing a new form of computer-assited psychotherapy (CAP) which is designed to be delivered in a group setting and is based upon the principles of cognitive-behavior therapy.

the development of a computerized treatment system, the Therapeutic Learning Program (TLP), that is intended to be an adjunct to the work of a clinician in providing cognitive-behavior therapy to groups of patients with anxiety and depression.
